newsitem.title: USA: McDonald's plans 20 pct profit growth outside U.S.
newsitem.headline: McDonald's plans 20 pct profit growth outside U.S.

text.p: McDonald's Corp said Friday it plans to grow international operating income at a compound annual rate of about 20 percent as measured over a five-year period.
It also set a target of growing international sales at a compound annual percentage rate in the mid to high teens.
"We enjoy a significant lead over the competition outside of the United States and plan to extend this lead through our convenience strategy," McDonald's Chairman Michael Quinlan said in a statement.
The convenience strategy for McDonald's includes opening restaurants close to where consumers live, work and shop.

"Our U.S. restaurants are operating in a complex, dynamic and difficult marketplace and recent operating performance has fallen short of our goals," Quinlan added. "Yet, we are very optimistic about our long-term opportunities to grow in the domestic marketplace."
He said McDonald's objective is to grow U.S. sales and operating income at a compound annual rate in the mid-single digits as measured over a five-year period.
"...(W)e intend to improve results to achieve this long-term objective," Quinlan added.
He said McDonald's will focus on four initiatives in the United States to improve performance, including food taste, quality of service, strategic marketing and adding new restaurants.
